sections.h2: Where to record a deed in Lancaster County
sections.html:
Send or carry deeds to the Recorder of Deeds, 150 North Queen Street, Suite 315, Lancaster, PA 17603. The office is open from 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. on weekdays, and recording itself concludes at 4:30 p.m.

Payments aren't taken over the phone. Since October 1, 2025, staff no longer print trusts or other supporting papers as a courtesy. Send those pages already printed, or attach them to an electronic filing, to avoid a 25 cent per page printing charge.

For a seller, this office comes at the very end. The deed is signed and acknowledged at closing, then recorded here, and the county's public search shows the new owner afterward.

The posted base fee for a deed or mortgage of up to four pages is $71.25. Every page after the fourth adds $2.00, and the office doesn't issue refunds.

Lancaster County base recording fees, up to four pages
Document typeBase fee
Deed or mortgage$71.25
Assignment, release, satisfaction, installment sale agreement, easement$59.75
Agreement, termination, modification, subordination$58.75
Power of attorney or deputation (miscellaneous)$18.50
Certification$10.00
Copies, per page$0.25

The JCP fee rose from $40.25 to $41.25 under Act 45 of 2025. Call the office for the exact total on your package.

A military discharge, the DD-214, is recorded free.

For recording, the counter accepts cash, certified checks, corporate checks, money orders and credit cards. Personal checks are refused for amounts over $75 and are never taken for transfer tax. Blank checks aren't accepted either.

  • Card payments carry a 2.5% charge on transactions over $50, and $1 on smaller ones.
  • A returned check costs $25.00.
  • There are no refunds, so the amount has to be right the first time.
  • Mailed or couriered packages need a self-addressed stamped envelope of the right size and with enough postage.

When a document type has no listed fee, the Recorder sets one. If your deed has attachments or several parcels, ask before sending money.

No cover page is needed, and staples are not allowed. Use white paper, 8.5 by 11, with type of 10 point or larger.

  • The notary acknowledgment date can't come before the date on the document, and the acknowledgment needs the state, county, date, the person appearing, the notary's signature and the notary's expiration date. The seal itself is optional for Pennsylvania notaries.
  • The tax parcel ID, with its district code, must appear on every deed.
  • Deeds, mortgages and assignments need a signed, certified address with a zip code for the buyer or lender. On a deed a P.O. box isn't allowed as that address, though the deed may say tax bills should go to a box.
  • Land in more than one municipality must state the percentage split of local transfer tax, in whole numbers.
  • Written amounts must match numbers, and no Social Security or bank account numbers should appear.
  • A transaction is limited to 10 documents, and blanket assignments or releases are rejected.

A corrective or confirmatory deed must come with a Statement of Value, an explanation, and a full copy of the deed it fixes.

You pay the tax to the Recorder when the deed is recorded. Pennsylvania takes 1 percent of the transferred value and treats buyer and seller as equally liable. Local taxes are collected at the same counter and divided between municipalities and school districts.

Some transfers are exempt: certain family transfers, transfers to governments, and property passing by will or intestacy. If the full tax isn't paid, attach a completed Statement of Value. The county counts that form as one page of the four-page base, and easements need one too.

If a deed names the wrong property location, the submitter bears the cost. The right municipality, school district and state must still be paid, and the submitter claims back anything sent to the wrong place.

The office handles mortgages, satisfactions, assignments, powers of attorney, leases, Uniform Commercial Code filings, notary commissions and military discharges. Several of these touch a house sale, so know the charges ahead of time.

  • A notary commission and bond costs $32.00, and registering the notary's signature adds $4.75.
  • Subdivision, stormwater and state highway plans start at $15.00 for the first page and add $2.00 per page. Condominium plans start at $30.00.
  • Plans must be at least 18 by 24 inches and no larger than 24 by 36, and both Mylar and paper are accepted.
  • A UCC-1 or UCC-3 filing costs $100.00 each.
  • Notaries can register their signature at the Recorder's office, which saves a trip to the Prothonotary's office in a separate building.

A seller paying off a mortgage should ask the lender when the satisfaction piece will be filed. At the posted $59.75 base, it is a separate recording with its own book and page reference back to the original mortgage.

sections.h2: Checklist before the deed leaves for the courthouse
sections.html:
Go through this list with the title agent.

  • Parcel ID and district code on the deed, matching the county record.
  • A certified buyer address that isn't a P.O. box.
  • Dollar figures that agree in words and numbers.
  • A completed Statement of Value if the transfer is taxed in part or exempt.
  • Payment in an accepted form: no personal check over $75 and none at all for transfer tax.
  • No staples and no cover sheet.

If the deed is going by mail, put the package together a few days early and enclose the return envelope. The office's public records search lets you confirm afterward that the deed appears under the buyer's name.

Once the package reaches the counter before 4:30 p.m., staff check it against the rules above, collect the fee and the transfer tax, and record it. If something is off, such as a stapled page, a P.O. box as the buyer's certified address or a personal check, the deed doesn't go on the record until it is fixed.

Fees aren't refunded, so a rejected package that needed a new payment form means a second trip or a second mailing. The sellers who avoid this are the ones whose title agent ran the checklist before sending anything. When the deed is recorded, the county's public search should show the new owner under the buyer's name.

A house that needs work can sell to a cash buyer without lender paperwork, but the recording side of the closing doesn't change.
Lancaster County had 563,159 residents and 223,178 housing units in July 2025. Owners live in 69.8% of homes for 2020 to 2024, at a median value of $301,100. Median gross rent is $1,357.

faqs.q: What is the base fee for a deed at the Lancaster County Recorder of Deeds?
faqs.a: The posted base fee is $71.25 for a deed or mortgage of up to four pages, plus $2.00 for each added page. The JCP fee rose to $41.25 under Act 45 of 2025, so confirm the total with the office.

faqs.q: Can I pay Lancaster County transfer tax with a personal check?
faqs.a: No. Personal checks are never accepted for transfer tax, and they are refused for any amount over $75. Use cash, a certified or corporate check, a money order or a credit card, with the card fee added.

faqs.q: Does a Lancaster County deed need a cover page?
faqs.a: No. Cover pages are no longer required, and staples must not be used. Use white 8.5 by 11 paper and type of at least 10 point.

faqs.q: Can I use a P.O. box as the buyer's address on a Lancaster County deed?
faqs.a: Not as the certified address, which must be a street address with a zip code. The deed may say that tax bills should be mailed to a P.O. box.

faqs.q: What time does the Lancaster County recorder stop recording?
faqs.a: Recording concludes at 4:30 p.m., though the office stays open until 5:00 p.m. on weekdays. Documents that come in after 4:30 p.m. wait for the next business day.
